title: Research method for Stroke effector gene predictions (Malik et al., 2018)
bodyHtml:
These results are from the study:

Multiancestry genome-wide association study of 520,000 subjects identifies 32 loci associated with stroke and stroke subtypes.
Malik R, Chauhan G, Traylor M, Sargurupremraj M, Okada Y, et al.
Nat Genet. 2018 Apr;50(4):524-537. doi: 10.1038/s41588-018-0058-3..
PMID: 29531354

Candidate effector genes for stroke were prioritized at loci with genome-wide significant associations for stroke, as discovered in a GWAS in up to 67,162 stroke cases and 454,450 controls. Each gene was assigned a biological score and an overall score, reflecting the number of evidence types supporting the prediction.

The biological score is the sum of individual scores (one point each) for the following evidence types:

  • Nearest gene: gene is the nearest gene to the lead SNP
  • Missense variant: the lead SNP causes a missense change in the gene
  • eQTL evidence: the lead SNP or a SNP in high LD with it is an eQTL for expression of the gene (see the "QTLs" row by clicking the View button to open the sub-table)
  • meQTL evidence: the lead SNP or a SNP in high LD with it is a methylation QTL for the gene (see the "QTLs" row by clicking the View button to open the sub-table)
  • pQTL evidence: the lead SNP or a SNP in high LD with it is a pQTL for protein levels of the gene product (see the "QTLs" row by clicking the View button to open the sub-table)
  • epiGWAS: SNPs associated with stroke, or their LD proxies, display cell type-specific enrichment in enhancer and promoter sites in any of 9 cell types (see the "epiGWAS" row by clicking the View button to open the sub-table) 

The overall score is the sum of the biological score plus individual scores (one point each) for the following evidence types (displayed in the "Pathway-Drug" row that is visible after clicking the View button to open the sub-table):

  • DEPICT pathway enrichment: the gene is annotated to a biological pathway that is overrepresented in the stroke genetic association results, as determined using the DEPICT method (Pers TH et al., 2015)
  • Ingenuity Pathway Analysis: the gene is annotated to a biological pathway that is overrepresented in the stroke genetic association results, as determined using Ingenuity Pathway Analysis
  • VEGAS2 pathway enrichment: the gene is annotated to a biological pathway that is overrepresented in the stroke genetic association results, as determined using the VEGAS2 method (Mishra and MacGregor, 2017)
  • ATC-C category: the gene is listed as a cardiovascular drug target in the DrugBank and Therapeutic Target (Yang H et al., 2016) databases
  • ATC-B01 category: the gene is listed as a antithrombotic drug target in the DrugBank and Therapeutic Target (Yang H et al., 2016) databases
